values.Background: The Trans-Arabian Pipeline (Tapline) was a crude oil pipeline running from Qaisumah in Saudi Arabia across Jordan, southern Syria (including the Golan Heights), and into Lebanon, terminating at the Sidon (Zahrani) Mediterranean export terminal. Constructed 1947-1950 by the Trans-Arabian Pipeline Company (a subsidiary of Aramco) using 30-inch and 31-inch steel pipe over a 1,213-1,214 km route, with six main pumping stations (Nariya, Qaisumah, Rafha, Badanah, Turaif in Saudi Arabia; Qaryatain in Jordan). Initial capacity 320,000 bpd, expanded via auxiliary pumping in 1957 to ~450,000 bpd and a peak nameplate of ~500,000 bpd. The cross-border line ceased operating in 1976 as the Lebanese Civil War began and supertankers eroded its economics; the Saudi and Jordanian portions continued intermittently until 1983/1990. Final 'de-cruding' (cleaning of residual crude) was completed in 2001. Designated Saudi Arabia's first industrial heritage site in December 2020.

resolutions.primary_value: The Trans-Arabian Pipeline (Tapline) was a crude oil pipeline running from Qaisumah in Saudi Arabia across Jordan, southern Syria (including the Golan Heights), and into Lebanon, terminating at the Sidon (Zahrani) Mediterranean export terminal. Constructed 1947-1950 by the Trans-Arabian Pipeline Company (a subsidiary of Aramco) using 30-inch and 31-inch steel pipe over a 1,213-1,214 km route, with six main pumping stations (Nariya, Qaisumah, Rafha, Badanah, Turaif in Saudi Arabia; Qaryatain in Jordan). Initial capacity 320,000 bpd, expanded via auxiliary pumping in 1957 to ~450,000 bpd and a peak nameplate of ~500,000 bpd. The cross-border line ceased operating in 1976 as the Lebanese Civil War began and supertankers eroded its economics; the Saudi and Jordanian portions continued intermittently until 1983/1990. resolutions.researcher_notes: Background is a composite narrative; its constituent facts (route Qaisumah->Sidon via Jordan/Syria/Lebanon, 1947-1950 construction, 30/31-in pipe, ~1,213 km, pumping stations, 320k->500k bpd capacity, cessation 1976/1990, de-cruding 2001, heritage-site designation) are spread across the cited sources. Existing Aramco URL is dead (timeout). Britannica/Saudipedia each cover most facts but the original deterministic check failed only because it matched the whole paragraph verbatim; substantively all four kept sources support the narrative. Added encyclopedia.com (covers capacity 320k/500k, Abqaiq supply, route, Aramco). NOTE divergence: Saudipedia gives total length 1,648 km and Britannica/EC give ~1,720 km total Al-Dammam-to-Sidon vs the 754 mi (1,213-1,214 km) Qaisumah-mainline figure used by GEM -- the 'Background' correctly distinguishes the mainline figure. Heritage-site (Dec 2020) and exact 1957 auxiliary-pumping detail are sourced from Aramco/gem narrative and not independently re-verified here (Aramco dead); flagged as the weakest sub-claims.

ProposalYear=1947 ties to the start of design/construction in 1947. Both existing refs are live but do NOT state 1947 (AUB finding aid is a collection catalog; encyclopedia.com gives only WWII/postwar context) -> DEAD_LINK. Replaced with 2 independent sources that state 1947: Wikipedia ('Construction of the Trans-Arabian Pipeline began in 1947') and aleqt Arabic ('في عام 1947، بدأ تصميم ثم إنشاء خط التابلاين' = in 1947, design then construction of the Tapline began). Note: sources frame 1947 as the design/construction-start year; if GEM intends 'Proposal' strictly as agreement/concession year this is a close proxy but worth a glance.

ConstructionYear=1948 is hard to corroborate at 2+ sources. The existing Aramco URL is dead (timeout); the AUB finding aid does not state a construction year. Only one independent source explicitly gives 1948: aleqt Arabic ('في عام 1948' for physical construction start, distinguishing it from the 1947 design year). CONFLICT/nuance: Wikipedia and Britannica state construction 'began in 1947' (managed by Bechtel), so the dominant English sources put the construction start a year earlier than GEM's 1948. Could not reach 2 independent sources for the literal value 1948 -> medium (single verified source), and flagged as a likely 1947-vs-1948 ambiguity (1947 = design/award + initial works; 1948 = main physical construction) for Update review.

StartYear1=1950 (oil first flowed / pipeline inaugurated) confirmed by 4 independent sources: Wikipedia ('active during 1950-1976'), encyclopedia.com ('began operations in 1950'), Saudipedia ('inaugurated in 1950'), aleqt Arabic ('انتهت أعمال إنشاء الأنبوب الرئيس ومرافق الضخ في عام 1950'). High confidence.

StopYear=1976 marks when the FULL cross-border line ceased operating (Lebanese Civil War). Only Wikipedia explicitly anchors 1976 ('The full length of the pipeline was active during 1950-1976'). The two other existing refs are live but do NOT state 1976: AUB finding aid (catalog, no year) and encyclopedia.com (gives 'early 1980s' and '1990', not 1976) -> DEAD_LINK on those two. CONFLICT: other sources emphasize different stop years -- encyclopedia.com 'largely ceased functioning in the early 1980s'/'completely stopped operating in 1990'; Saudipedia/Aramco 'decommissioned in 1990'; aleqt 'توقف بعدها الخط تماما في أوائل التسعينيات' (~1990s). 1976 = cross-border shutdown, 1983/1990 = full decommissioning; GEM's StopYear=1976 reflects the cross-border line. Reached only 1 verified source for the literal 1976 value -> medium; flagged the 1976-vs-1990 distinction for Update.

Capacity=500,000 bpd (peak) confirmed by 3 independent sources: Wikipedia ('maximum capacity of about 500,000 bbl/d'), encyclopedia.com ('Tapline's capacity in 2003 was 500,000 barrels per day'), aleqt Arabic ('ارتفعت في وقت لاحق إلى 500 ألف برميل في اليوم' = later rose to 500,000 bpd). High. NOTE: Britannica states an erroneous 'initial capacity of 3 million barrels per day' (clear typo for 300,000) and was therefore NOT used for this unit. Initial capacity was ~300,000-320,000 bpd across sources; GEM uses the peak 500,000.

LengthKnown=1,214 km (the mainline section) confirmed by 3 independent sources: Wikipedia ('1,214 kilometres (754 mi) long'), encyclopedia.com ('754 miles (1,213 km) of the pipeline'), Britannica ('754 miles (1,213 km)'). High. NOTE divergence on TOTAL system length: Britannica/EC give ~1,069 mi (1,720 km) Al-Dammam-to-Sidon including the gathering section, and Saudipedia gives 1,648 km -- GEM's 1,214 km correctly uses the 754-mi mainline (Qaisumah-to-Sidon) figure, consistent across all three kept refs.

Diameter=30 and 31 inches confirmed by 2 independent sources: Britannica ('30-inch (760-mm) and 31-inch (790-mm) pipe') and Wikipedia ('diameter of 30 inches (760 mm) and 31 inches'). Kept Britannica (live + value present), dropped the dead Aramco URL (timeout), added Wikipedia as the 2nd independent corroboration -> DEAD_LINK (replacement done). CONFLICT noted but not used: aleqt Arabic gives '30 و32 بوصة' (30 and 32 inch), which disagrees with the 31-inch figure; the two English encyclopedic sources agree on 30/31, so GEM's value stands.

FuelSource=Abqaiq, Saudi Arabia (oil fields feeding the line) confirmed by 3 independent sources: encyclopedia.com ('carry crude oil from Abqaiq, Saudi Arabia'), Wikipedia ('supplied from the oil fields near Abqaiq'), aleqt Arabic ('خطوط الأنابيب القادمة من بقيق' = pipelines coming from Abqaiq). High.

StartLocation=Qaisumah, Saudi Arabia confirmed by 3 independent sources: Wikipedia ('oil pipeline from Qaisumah in Saudi Arabia'), encyclopedia.com ('315-mile portion from Al-Dammam to Al-Qaysumah' -- Qaisumah is the start of the 754-mi mainline that GEM tracks), aleqt Arabic ('القيصومة'). High. Qaisumah is the junction where the gathering lines from Abqaiq/Al-Dammam meet the mainline; consistent across sources.

EndLocation=Sidon Terminal (Zahrani), Lebanon confirmed by 3 independent sources: Wikipedia ('to Sidon in Lebanon'), Britannica ('to Sidon, Lebanon, on the Mediterranean Sea'), encyclopedia.com ('its western terminus a few miles south of Sidon, Lebanon'). High. The Zahrani terminal sits just south of Sidon, matching the GEM 'Sidon Terminal' value.

Owner has NO [ref] column -- these citations go to ResearcherNotes, not a [ref] cell. Ownership (Trans-Arabian Pipeline Co., a wholly owned subsidiary of Aramco; now Saudi Aramco / Saudi Arabian Oil Co.) confirmed by 3 independent sources: Wikipedia ('built and operated by the Trans-Arabian Pipeline Company ... now a fully owned subsidiary of Aramco'), Britannica ('built by a subsidiary of the Arabian American Oil Company (Aramco)'), encyclopedia.com ('constructed by the Arabian American Oil Company (ARAMCO)'). High. Historical nuance for ResearcherNotes: Tapline was originally a JV of the four Aramco partners (Standard Oil of NJ/CA, Texaco, Socony-Vacuum) before becoming a fully owned Aramco subsidiary; today succeeded by Saudi Aramco -- consistent with the GEM Owner/Parent values.

Fuel=Oil confirmed. Offshore Technology titles/describes it as an 'oil pipeline' for the Marjan field; OilEnergy Digital (oedigital) and the Arabic Sinopec coverage describe crude-oil/oilfield pipelines for the Marjan field. Two independent publishers (GlobalData vs OE Digital). High.

Existing ref (newarab) is live (verifier HTTP 200, expected content present); WebFetch returns 403 to its browser UA but the source is genuine — documents the Chinese (Sinopec) contract win for the Marjan expansion, supporting an active/under-construction project. Added a 2nd independent corroborator (Offshore Technology) which states the pipeline is in the 2021-2025 build window and 'expected to commence operations in 2025' (i.e. under construction). Two independent publishers. REVERIFIED, high.

ProposalYear=2019 supported by the July 2019 contract-award coverage: Asharq Al-Awsat (Arabic, dated 2019, $18bn awards to expand Marjan/Berri incl. new crude pipelines) and Offshore (offshore-mag, 2019, 34 contracts / $18bn). Two independent outlets. Note: GEM's ProposalYear is a proxy for the 2019 award/sanction of the expansion program; the field program itself was first announced ~2017 (per nsenergybusiness/Worley FEED 2017) — if GEM intends 'first proposed', 2017 is defensible too. Flagging the ambiguity; 2019 (the EPC award) is well-sourced. High.

ConstructionYear=2021 is supported only by Offshore Technology (GlobalData), which gives the pipeline capex window as 2021-2025 (implying construction start ~2021). No independent 2nd source pins the pipeline construction-start to 2021 specifically — the field/Tanajib gas-plant works started 2020, but that is the plant, not this pipeline. Single source (GlobalData family). Medium / yellow — needs a 2nd independent corroborator.

StartYear1=2025 well corroborated. Zawya project-update: Marjan/Berri crude increments 'expected to be onstream by 2025'. Offshore Technology: pipeline 'expected to commence operations in 2025'. Independent publishers (Refinitiv/Zawya vs GlobalData); also consistent with the 2019 Arabic award coverage citing a 2025 target. High. (Note: the pipeline is part of the field increment; 2025 = expected commissioning of the increment it serves.)

Capacity=300,000 bpd corroborated by Asharq Al-Awsat (Arabic: 300,000 b/d Arab medium crude from Marjan) and Offshore (offshore-mag: 'increase production from the Marjan field by 300,000 b/d of Arabian medium crude'). Two independent outlets. CAVEAT: this 300,000 bpd is the Marjan FIELD increment capacity, not an independently published throughput for this specific pipeline; GEM uses it as the pipeline's capacity. Defensible but document the field-vs-pipe distinction. High for the figure as stated.

Length=100 km stated only by Offshore Technology (GlobalData). CONFLICT: its sister GlobalData publication NS Energy (nsenergybusiness) describes '70km of 36in-diameter oil export pipelines' for the same expansion — so the figure is single-publisher AND internally inconsistent (100km vs 70km). No truly independent source confirms 100km. Low / needs review — recommend Update revisit whether 100km is the right value or whether 70km (export pipeline) is intended. No 2nd independent corroborator found.

Diameter=36 in stated by Offshore Technology ('maximum diameter of 36 inches') and by sister title NS Energy ('70km of 36in-diameter oil export pipelines'). Both are GlobalData/Mike-Danson media-group properties, so they are NOT independent of each other — effectively one source. Medium / single-source. No independent 2nd confirmation of the 36in figure found.

FuelSource=Marjan Oil Field confirmed. Offshore Technology names the Marjan field as the source; OE Digital states the pipelines serve 'Saudi Aramco's Marjan oilfield'; Arabic coverage (zawya/aawsat) likewise refers to 'حقل المرجان النفطي' (the Marjan oil field). Multiple independent outlets. High.

StartLocation=Persian/Arabian Gulf (Saudi Arabia) stated by Offshore Technology ('start in the Arabian Gulf (Saudi Arabia)'). Consistent with the field being an offshore Marjan-field pipeline (Group B/C describe offshore Marjan field, Tanajib). Only one source explicitly names the start point as the Gulf, so medium / single-source for the precise StartLocation. Persian Gulf == Arabian Gulf (same body of water).

EndLocation=Eastern Province (Saudi Arabia) stated by Offshore Technology ('end in the Eastern Province (Saudi Arabia)'). Consistent with onshore processing at Tanajib, which is in the Eastern Province (Group B/C name Tanajib/Ras Tanura as the onshore destination). Only Offshore Technology names 'Eastern Province' verbatim, so medium / single-source for the precise wording.

Cost=$204m stated only by Offshore Technology ('estimated capex of $204m' over 2021-2025) — a GlobalData modeled capex, not an awarded contract value. No independent 2nd source publishes a $204m pipeline cost (the widely cited $18bn is the whole Marjan+Berri program, not this pipe). Single-source / medium. Recommend Update treat as a GlobalData estimate.

Owner=Saudi Aramco (100%) confirmed. Offshore Technology lists owner as 'Saudi Arabian Oil' (Aramco); OE Digital/Egypt Oil & Gas/Arabic coverage all describe the pipeline as belonging to 'Saudi Aramco's Marjan oilfield'. Two+ independent outlets. Owner has NO [ref] column — this corroboration goes to ResearcherNotes, not a [ref] cell. High.
